problems: The title and caption promise a wheel you can see through, but in the picture a dark solid disc (the drum or motor behind it) fills almost the whole space between the arms. What you see through the wheel is another brown disc, so the openness is hard to read.
The caption mentions 'four arms through a hub', but a wooden upright stands right in front of the hub and covers it along with the inner ends of the arms. You can't count four arms or see a hub.
The caption says 'pale hornbeam cogs', but the cogs are a dull grey-olive that is barely different from the oak rim. Nothing in the picture tells two woods apart.
The wheel's teeth mesh with nothing. No pinion, lantern or drum gear touches them, so a toothed wheel sits on the block with no visible job and the caption gives it none.

The lower edge of the wheel seems to run down into the top of the block. The bottom cogs (around the lower middle of the picture) disappear into the block top, so it looks like it clips through instead of resting on a bearing.
A thin rod or rope comes out of the lower-left of the wheel and runs diagonally down the side of the block. It doesn't connect to anything you can make sense of.

The block is a plain, untextured brown octagonal prism, and the table and posts around it are flat brown boxes. The detailed wheel sits among bare shapes. A big table in the upper left and the post in front of the hub take up much of the frame, and the wheel only fills the middle third.
posts.critique: The caption describes a millwright's open wheel with four arms, a hub and pale hornbeam cogs. The picture shows grey-olive cogs on a rim backed by a dark disc, with a post hiding the hub, no gear for the teeth to engage, and a bottom edge that seems to sink into a featureless block. You can't check most of what the caption claims, and the part you can see looks unfinished.
